label: federal
design: The register of U.S. government digital services: navy and white, a thin red rule, heavy underlined links, high contrast, nothing decorative. Wide comfortable line height. Should feel like a page built to be read by anyone on any device, because that is the actual constraint of the work it describes.
language: Direct and unadorned. Short paragraphs. Say who is affected. Avoid agency jargon and avoid vendor polish equally — federal readers distrust both.
note: Evokes the visual register of government services because that is the domain of the work described. Uses no seal, agency mark, or official identifier, and carries Alex's own masthead and byline throughout. It is a portfolio page about his work, not a government page.
